newsitem.title: HUNGARY: NN HUNGARY SEES PREMIUM UP, HAS NEW PRODUCT.
newsitem.headline: NN HUNGARY SEES PREMIUM UP, HAS NEW PRODUCT.

text.p: Nationale Nederlanden Hungary Ltd generated a 1.21 billion forint after-tax profit and a 17.359 billion forints premium revenues in 1996, becoming one of the fastest-growing members of the ING Group .

"ING Group's (annual) report picks out two countries performing outsandingly in life insurance, these are Japan and Hungary," Gyorgy Bordas, chairman and CEO of NN Hungary, told a news conference on Tuesday.
For 1997 the insurance company forecasts premium revenues of 22 billion forints, Bordas said. He declined to give a profit plan but said NN wanted to exceed last year's profit.
Bordas added that NN Hungary, with a 36 percent market share in life insurance, sought to increase the number of its clients to some 350,000 by the end of 1997, from the current 300,000 plus.
To further strengthen its position, NN Hungary has launched a new product, offering the first ever unit-linked life insurance in Hungary, linked to investment funds, Bordas said.
"The new life insurance...is a savings product which supplements the insurance with bond and share investments," NN Hungary said in a statement.
Hungary's total 1996 premium revenues are estimated at 150 billion forints.
In terms of premium revenues NN Hungary ranked the fourth position last year, but unlike the first three insurance firms, is involved in life insurance only.
